novelty.justification: The core new-mechanism hypothesis is that "the same hierarchical-syntax circuit [is] reused when the model reasons over non-linguistic hierarchical structure," specifically predicting selective, depth-dependent causal involvement across arithmetic, Boolean logic, parentheses, and code rather than merely another syntax localization result. Searches under "LLM syntax circuit arithmetic reasoning activation patching," "hierarchical syntax circuit non-linguistic reasoning transformer," and "shared circuits syntax math code LLM" identify Causal Head Gating (2025) as the closest work because it causally analyzes heads across syntax and mathematical reasoning, while Separating Tongue from Thought (2024) studies cross-language representational sharing; neither advances the specific syntax-derived-circuit reuse and nesting-depth relationship claimed here. Moving from those task-wise localization and representation-sharing studies to a causal claim that one language-localized hierarchy mechanism serves as a general cross-domain structure engine requires a new core relationship rather than a direct transfer, although the broader shared hierarchical-processing idea has precedents in cognitive-science accounts such as Fitch's The Evolution of Syntax: An Exaptationist Perspective (2011), keeping this at high within-framework novelty rather than paradigm-level novelty.
